items.title: Ship categorisation and merchant enrichment gated on the deterministic baseline
items.outcome: As a user, my transactions are categorised more accurately than the rule-based system managed, and whenever I disagree my correction wins and stays won.
items.context: Model categorisation is only worth its cost and risk if it measurably beats the deterministic baseline that already exists. Without that gate the product takes on model risk for no gain, and users experience regressions on categories the rules used to get right.
scope: Categorisation pipeline routed to the cheap model tier
Merchant enrichment reusing the normalised dictionary rather than inventing names
Comparison against the deterministic baseline on the golden corpus before replacement
User override that persists and takes precedence permanently
Confidence routing so low-confidence results go to the clarification queue instead of being applied
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline beats the deterministic baseline on the golden corpus before it replaces it, and the comparison is recorded
A user override persists, wins over any later model result and is auditable
Categorisation never touches the expensive model tier, verified by a routing assertion
Low-confidence results are routed to clarification rather than silently applied
Enrichment never invents a merchant name absent from the dictionary without marking it as unverified
Disabling the feature returns the system to the deterministic baseline with no data migration
contracts_schema: Consumes the published tool and clarification contracts; results are written through the existing ingestion path
security_privacy: Merchant strings are minimised before any external call
No categorisation result is trusted enough to move money or change a balance
observability: Publishes accuracy against the corpus, override rate and routing tier distribution
tests: Baseline comparison on the golden corpus
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag, enabled per cohort after the baseline comparison passes
Rollback returns to the deterministic baseline immediately with no data loss
non_goals: Numeric answers of any kind, which the provenance ticket governs
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo ai-service. Owns the pipeline. Overrides are stored by the api through the existing contract.

items.title: Enforce numeric provenance and ship grounded question answering with citations and insights
items.outcome: As a user, every figure the assistant shows me is traceable to my own data, every claim links to the records it came from, and the assistant refuses rather than guesses when it cannot ground an answer.
items.context: The single unrecoverable failure for a finance assistant is a confidently wrong number. Provenance enforcement is what makes that structurally impossible: a response containing a figure absent from tool output is blocked before it reaches the user.
scope: Post-processing that rejects any figure absent from tool output
Grounded answering that cites the user's own records for each claim
A path from any answer to the full calculation behind it
Proactive insights derived from deterministic aggregates with hedged language
Batched periodic reviews generated off-peak for cost
Refusal behaviour when grounding is unavailable
Goal and debt narrative explanations generated only from deterministic projection output and its provenance
Weekly and monthly review narratives generated from deterministic aggregates with an explicit as-of time
acceptance_criteria: A response containing a figure not present in tool output is blocked and alerted, proven by an injected test case
Every claim links to the source records and the link resolves to data the user owns
An answer that cannot be grounded produces an explicit refusal rather than a plausible guess
Insights are derived from aggregates and never assert causation
Batched reviews are skipped for inactive users and their cost per run is tracked against the model
Figures shown are never rounded away from the values the tools returned
Every goal or debt narrative links to the deterministic calculation and is refused when provenance is incomplete
Periodic reviews state their covered interval and as-of time and contain no figure absent from tool output
contracts_schema: Consumes the tool contract; provenance identifiers from tool results are carried through to the response
security_privacy: Grounding data is scoped by the tool layer, so a compromised prompt cannot widen the source set
Citations reference records the requesting user owns and nothing else
observability: Publishes provenance rejection counts, refusal rate and cost per active user
tests: Goal and debt narrative provenance tests
Periodic review interval, as-of time and unsupported-figure rejection tests
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per surface; provenance enforcement is never optional and ships with the first surface
Rollback disables the surface rather than relaxing provenance
non_goals: Any arithmetic performed by the model, which is prohibited by design
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo ai-service. Owns provenance enforcement and answer construction. All figures originate from the api tool layer.

items.title: Build the Android assistant surfaces with disclosure, override, refusal and advice-boundary guardrails
items.outcome: As a user, I always know when I am reading model output, I can contest or override anything it produced, and it declines to tell me what to buy or invest in rather than crossing into regulated advice.
items.context: The regulatory boundary is that the product is a calculator and a mirror, never an adviser, and the debt wedge fortunately sits outside the sensitive scope. The controls have to be visible in the interface, because the obligation is about what the user is told, not what the server intended.
scope: Disclosure on every surface where model output appears
Disclaimer rendering driven by the versioned compliance text rather than local copy
Contest and override controls on any model-produced categorisation or narrative
Refusal presentation that explains why rather than failing silently
Banned-term scan in the build for creditworthiness-adjacent and product-recommendation language
Clarification assistance integrated with the existing inbox without nagging
BYOK and custom-endpoint registration, validation, replacement and revocation through backend APIs only
Plan quota usage, reset time and provider status without exposing key material
T-AIP-05 natural-language transaction draft review, correction and explicit confirmation through the normal transaction API
History-off state plus opt-in thread list, provenance, expiry, export and per-thread or bulk deletion using T-CON-14
acceptance_criteria: Every surface showing model output carries the disclosure and the current disclaimer version
A user can contest any model output and the override persists and is auditable
A refusal is presented in plain language with a route to the deterministic answer where one exists
The build fails if banned terminology appears in user-facing copy
Suggestions are batched and never interrupt the user repeatedly for the same item
All assistant surfaces are screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
The Android client never calls a provider endpoint directly and never receives a stored provider key back
A revoked or replaced key and a disabled custom endpoint produce a clear recoverable state
Adding or changing a key or endpoint requires a fresh passkey step-up; risk-triggered changes show their twenty-four-hour pending window, notification channel and cancellation action
After account recovery, suspended provider configuration is explained and must be re-enrolled rather than silently reactivated
A natural-language draft cannot write until every field is visible and the user explicitly confirms
History is off by default; enabling it shows retention, persisted threads are accessible and deletable, and ephemeral turns never appear later
contracts_schema: Consumes the published assistant contract and the versioned disclaimer identifier
security_privacy: Model output is never presented as authoritative for a monetary figure without its provenance link
No assistant surface fires analytics containing message or transaction content
observability: Records disclosure impressions and override actions without content
tests: Disclosure presence test on every surface
Banned-term build scan with planted copy
BYOK and custom-endpoint registration, replacement and revocation instrumented tests
Step-up expiry, pending activation, notification cancellation and post-recovery re-enrollment tests
Natural-language draft correction, confirmation, expiry and cancellation tests
History-off no-reappearance, thread export and accessible deletion tests
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per surface, enabled only after the refusal suite and provenance enforcement are green
Rollback hides the surface and leaves deterministic screens untouched
non_goals: Server-side guardrails, which the ai-service tickets own

items.title: Build the web assistant with citations, disclosure, BYOK and custom-endpoint management
items.outcome: As a user, I can ask the assistant a question in natural language on the web and get an answer with citations, derivation and a refusal when appropriate, I can bring my own provider key or register a custom endpoint with it validated before acceptance and revocable at any time, and I can see my current quota status.
items.context: This mirrors the disclosure and guardrail obligations T-AIP-03 already built for Android, and extends T-AIP-02's grounded, provenance-carrying answering to the web surface. It also exposes the bring-your-own-key and custom-endpoint registration that T-AI-03's adversarial validation suite exists to defend, so registration, validation and revocation all have to be visible and reversible from the same surface that shows billing quota.
scope: Natural-language entry point for the assistant with citation, derivation and refusal presentation
Bring-your-own-key registration flow that stores the key only through the gateway's envelope encryption and never in browser storage
Custom-endpoint registration that runs the request through the existing adversarial validation suite before it is accepted
Explicit revocation control for any registered key or endpoint
Fresh passkey step-up and risk-triggered pending-activation experience showing the activation time, verified notification and cancellation control
Post-recovery suspended state requiring re-enrollment rather than automatic reuse
Quota status display sourced from the same billing quota state the customer billing portal surfaces
Disclaimer rendered on every assistant surface from the versioned compliance text
T-AIP-05 natural-language transaction draft review with every parsed field, correction, cancellation, expiry and explicit confirmation through the normal transaction API
History-off state plus opt-in thread list, provenance, expiry, export and per-thread or bulk deletion using T-CON-14
acceptance_criteria: Every assistant answer carries its citations and provenance links
A refusal is presented in plain language with a route to a deterministic answer where one exists
A bring-your-own-key is never observable from browser script storage or client-side logs, proven by a test
A custom endpoint targeting a disallowed destination, such as a private or loopback address, fails registration
Revoking a key or endpoint takes effect before the next assistant request completes
A stale step-up cannot submit a change, and a pending change cannot be used before its activation time
The verified-channel notification opens a cancellation path that remains usable without exposing the key or full endpoint
After account recovery, every prior provider configuration is visibly suspended and cannot be reactivated without fresh enrollment

A natural-language request cannot write financial state until every T-CON-16 draft field is visible and the user explicitly confirms; cancellation or expiry writes nothing and a retried confirmation creates one transaction
Quota status shown matches the server figure exactly, and keyboard, screen-reader and two-hundred-percent zoom users can complete every assistant action
History is off by default; enabling it shows retention, persisted threads are keyboard accessible and deletable, and ephemeral turns never reappear
contracts_schema: Consumes the published assistant contract, the billing quota contract and the versioned disclaimer identifier
security_privacy: Bring-your-own-key material is held only in the encrypted gateway path and never reaches application logs or analytics
Custom-endpoint validation reuses the existing adversarial request-forgery suite rather than a lighter web-only check
observability: Records assistant interaction outcomes, registration and revocation events and quota status views without content or key material
tests: Browser-storage exposure test for bring-your-own-key material
Step-up expiry, risk-triggered cooling-off, notification cancellation and recovery-suspension tests
Browser-matrix compatibility test across the supported browser set
Natural-language draft correction, cancellation, expiry and idempotent-confirmation tests
History-off no-reappearance, export and deletion propagation tests
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind a flag enabled only after the adversarial validation suite and browser-storage exposure test are green
Rollback hides the assistant entry point and revokes no existing key or endpoint registration
non_goals: Server-side routing, failover and evaluation gating, which the ai-service tickets own
Native mobile assistant surfaces, which the Android ticket owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns the assistant surface and the key and endpoint management interface. Validation and gateway enforcement remain owned by ai-service.

items.title: Build confirmation-gated natural-language transaction entry
items.outcome: As a user, I can describe a transaction in ordinary language, review a complete structured draft, and explicitly confirm it through the normal transaction API without the model ever writing data or initiating a payment.
items.context: Natural-language entry is promised by the product specification but the AI tool surface is intentionally read-only. A draft-only parser preserves that safety boundary: the model proposes fields, the client shows them, and the existing deterministic transaction path performs the confirmed write.
scope: Natural-language parsing into a versioned structured transaction draft with confidence per field
Explicit refusal or clarification when amount, currency, direction, account or date is ambiguous
Draft expiry and one-time confirmation token that cannot itself create a transaction
Hostile-text handling that cannot change tool allowlists, system policy or user scope
Bounded retention and deletion of the original text after the draft policy window
acceptance_criteria: No model or AI endpoint can create, edit, delete, settle or pay a transaction
Every parsed field is visible to the user before confirmation and low-confidence fields require correction
Confirmation submits the reviewed fields through the ordinary idempotent transaction API
A hostile input cannot invoke an unapproved tool or alter the user scope, proven by an adversarial corpus
Expired or replayed confirmation tokens are rejected without creating a ledger effect
Original text is absent from logs, traces and retained records after the bounded policy window
contracts_schema: Consumes the structured capture contract from T-CON-02 and publishes a draft envelope with per-field confidence, expiry and a one-time confirmation token
The draft contract contains no operation capable of writing a transaction
security_privacy: Original text is treated as hostile and sensitive, minimized before inference and never used as an instruction
Confirmation requires the authenticated user and cannot widen account or tenant scope
observability: Publishes draft completion, clarification, refusal, expiry and confirmation counts without text or monetary values
tests: Negative test proving the AI service has no ledger-write capability
Load test for bounded draft parsing latency without retaining request content
rollout_rollback: Behind a per-surface flag and enabled only after the injection and no-write suites are green
Rollback disables draft creation; confirmed transactions already written through the normal API remain unchanged
non_goals: Initiating a payment, settlement or transfer, permanently
Committing a transaction without an explicit user review and confirmation
Voice transcription, which may feed this text contract later but is not implemented here
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo ai-service. Owns text-to-draft parsing and the draft contract implementation; clients own review and confirmation while api owns the ordinary transaction write.
